findings.bug: After loading a state machine by id, it caches the Item into the id-keyed map stateMachineMapById using a NAME_TENANT key (name+"_"+tenantId) instead of the id, so the id-map is polluted with a wrong-typed key and the name/tenant cache is never populated.
findings.why_real: The sibling method getStateMachine(name,tenant) at line 110 does the symmetric correct thing: it caches into the OTHER map (stateMachineMapById) using the id key (stateMachine.getId()). getStateMachineById should mirror that and put a name_tenant key into stateMachineMapByNameAndTenant, not into stateMachineMapById.
findings.how_to_prove: Configure a stateLangStore returning a StateMachine with id="m1", name="N", tenant="T". Call getStateMachineById("m1"). Assert stateMachineMapByNameAndTenant.containsKey("N_T") -> expected true, actual false; assert stateMachineMapById.containsKey("N_T") -> expected false, actual true.

findings.bug: encode() writes three trailing bytes (branchType, status code, lockStatus code at lines 385-388) but decode() only reads branchType and status and never reads the lockStatus byte, so a persisted/reloaded BranchSession always loses its lockStatus (silently defaults to Locked).
findings.why_real: encode() at lines 387-388 emits both status.getCode() and lockStatus.getCode(); a correct decode round-trip must consume both. decode() stops after status (line 546), leaving the lockStatus byte unread. GlobalSession.encode/decode is symmetric and reads every field it writes, establishing the round-trip contract.
findings.how_to_prove: Create BranchSession, setLockStatus(LockStatus.Rollbacking), encode() to bytes; new BranchSession().decode(bytes); assert getLockStatus()==Rollbacking -> expected Rollbacking, actual Locked.

findings.bug: On the incompatible-parameter-type error branch the log statement dereferences ret[i].getClass(), but ret[i] has never been assigned (still null) at that point, causing a NullPointerException instead of logging the offending value's class.
findings.why_real: Inside the branch guarded by (value != null && !parameterType.isAssignableFrom(value.getClass())), ret[i] has not yet been written (assignment only happens at line 99 in the else branch), so ret[i] is null and ret[i].getClass() throws NPE. The intended reference is value.getClass().
findings.how_to_prove: Invoke getArgValues so that getArgValue returns a value whose class is not assignable to the declared parameterType (e.g. declared type Integer, resolved value a String). Expected: error is logged and ret[i] set to null; actual: NullPointerException thrown from the LOGGER.error argument.

findings.bug: hash() calls instance.update(key.getBytes()) and then instance.digest(key.getBytes(UTF_8)); digest(input) performs a final update of input before digesting, so the SHA-256 is computed over key concatenated with itself (key||key) rather than over key.
findings.why_real: MessageDigest.digest(byte[] input) is documented to perform a final update with input then complete the hash. Combined with the preceding update(key), the digest input is key twice, which is not the plain SHA-256 of key. The correct pattern is a single update+digest() or digest(key) alone.
findings.how_to_prove: Compute reference = first 8 bytes of MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest("abc".getBytes(UTF_8)) folded to long; compare with SHA256Hash.hash("abc"). Expected equal; actual differs because the class hashes "abcabc".
